source.text: Παῦλος δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα, τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, δι’ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Paul, slave of Christ Jesus, called apostle, having been set apart for gospel of God, \v 2 which he promised beforehand through the prophets of him in writings holy \v 3 concerning the Son of him, the [one] having come from seed of David according to flesh, \v 4 the [one] having been appointed Son of God in power according to spirit of holiness from resurrection of dead [ones], Jesus Christ the Lord of us, \v 5 through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations on behalf of the name of him, \v 6 among whom are also you called of Jesus Christ, \v 7 to all the [ones] being in Rome beloved of God, called holy [ones]; grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Paul, a slave of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, called [to be] an apostle, set apart for [the] gospel of God, \v 2 which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised beforehand through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets in [the] holy Scriptures, \v 3 concerning {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, who came from [the] seed of David according to [the] flesh, \v 4 who was appointed Son of God in power according to [the] Spirit of holiness from [the] resurrection of [the] dead, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} our Lord, \v 5 through whom we received grace and apostleship for [the] obedience of faith among all the nations on behalf of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \v 6 among whom are you also, called [to belong] to Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 7 to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called [to be] holy ones: grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: From Paul, a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God. \v 2 God promised this gospel long ago through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets in the holy Scriptures. \v 3 It concerns {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, who by human descent was born of the line of David, \v 4 and who was appointed Son of God in power, through the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection of the dead: Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord. \v 5 Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have received grace and apostleship, to bring about the obedience of faith among all the nations for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \v 6 You are among them, you whom Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has called to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. \v 7 To all of you in Rome whom God loves and has called to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people: grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: This letter is from Paul. I am a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. God called me to be an apostle and chose me to tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good news. \v 2 Long ago God promised this good news through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, and their promises are written in the holy Scriptures. \v 3 The good news is about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. As a human being, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was born into the family line of King David. \v 4 Through the Holy Spirit, God appointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be the Son of God with power when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead. He is Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, our Lord. \v 5 Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God has given us grace and sent us out as apostles. We are sent to people of all the nations, so that they will come to faith and obey God. We do this for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \v 6 You are among those people too. Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has called you to belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 So I am writing to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has called you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people. May God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} give you grace and peace.

es.L: Pablo, esclavo {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}, llamado [a ser] apóstol, apartado para [el] evangelio de Dios, \v 2 que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} prometió de antemano por medio de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} profetas en [las] Escrituras santas, \v 3 acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, que vino de [la] descendencia de David según [la] carne, \v 4 que fue constituido Hijo de Dios en poder según [el] Espíritu de santidad a partir de [la] resurrección de [los] muertos, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor, \v 5 por medio de quien recibimos gracia y apostolado para [la] obediencia de [la] fe entre todas las naciones a favor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre, \v 6 entre las cuales {{plural_you:están|estáis}} también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, llamados [a pertenecer] a {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, \v 7 a todos los que están en Roma, amados de Dios, llamados [a ser] santos: gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz de Dios nuestro Padre y [del] Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: De Pablo, siervo {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}, llamado a ser apóstol y apartado para el evangelio de Dios. \v 2 Dios prometió este evangelio hace mucho tiempo por medio de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} profetas en las santas Escrituras. \v 3 Trata de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, que como hombre nació del linaje de David \v 4 y que fue constituido Hijo de Dios con poder, por el Espíritu de santidad, mediante la resurrección de los muertos: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor. \v 5 Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hemos recibido gracia y apostolado, para que entre todas las naciones haya obediencia de fe, para honra de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre. \v 6 Entre ellas {{plural_you:están|estáis}} también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a quienes {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} ha llamado para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}. \v 7 A todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en Roma, a quienes Dios ama y ha llamado a ser {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo santo: gracia y paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte de Dios nuestro Padre y del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Esta carta es de Pablo. Soy siervo {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}. Dios me llamó a ser apóstol y me escogió para anunciar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} buena noticia. \v 2 Hace mucho tiempo, Dios prometió esta buena noticia por medio de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} profetas, y esas promesas están escritas en las santas Escrituras. \v 3 La buena noticia trata de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. Como ser humano, nació en la familia del rey David. \v 4 Por medio del Espíritu Santo, Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} estableció como Hijo de Dios con poder cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} resucitó de entre los muertos. Él es {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor. \v 5 Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, Dios nos ha dado gracia y nos ha enviado como apóstoles. Nos envía a gente de todas las naciones, para que lleguen a creer y obedezcan a Dios. Lo hacemos para honrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre. \v 6 {{plural_you:Ustedes también están|Vosotros también estáis}} entre esa gente. {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha llamado para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}. \v 7 Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo a todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en Roma. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} ama y {{plural_you:los|os}} ha llamado a ser {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo santo. Que Dios nuestro Padre y el Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} {{plural_you:les|os}} den gracia y paz.

fr.L: Paul, esclave du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, appelé [à être] apôtre, mis à part pour l’Évangile de Dieu, \v 2 qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis d’avance par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prophètes dans les saintes Écritures, \v 3 au sujet de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, issu de la descendance de David selon la chair, \v 4 établi Fils de Dieu avec puissance selon l’Esprit de sainteté par la résurrection des morts, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} notre Seigneur, \v 5 par qui nous avons reçu grâce et apostolat pour l’obéissance de la foi parmi toutes les nations, pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, \v 6 parmi lesquelles vous êtes, vous aussi, appelés [à appartenir] à Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 7 à tous ceux qui sont à Rome, bien-aimés de Dieu, appelés [à être] saints : grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, serviteur du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, appelé à être apôtre et mis à part pour l’Évangile de Dieu. \v 2 Cet Évangile, Dieu l’avait promis depuis longtemps par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prophètes dans les saintes Écritures. \v 3 Il concerne {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, qui, comme homme, est issu de la lignée de David, \v 4 et qui a été établi Fils de Dieu avec puissance, par l’Esprit de sainteté, par la résurrection des morts : Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} notre Seigneur. \v 5 Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, nous avons reçu la grâce et l’apostolat, afin d’amener toutes les nations à l’obéissance de la foi, pour l’honneur de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. \v 6 Vous êtes de leur nombre, vous que Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a appelés à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenir. \v 7 À vous tous qui êtes à Rome, que Dieu aime et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a appelés à être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint : grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul. Je suis serviteur du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Dieu m’a appelé à être apôtre et m’a choisi pour annoncer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonne nouvelle. \v 2 Il y a longtemps, Dieu a promis cette bonne nouvelle par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} prophètes, et leurs promesses sont écrites dans les saintes Écritures. \v 3 Cette bonne nouvelle parle de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. Comme être humain, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est né dans la famille du roi David. \v 4 Par l’Esprit Saint, Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a établi Fils de Dieu avec puissance quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité d’entre les morts. C’est Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, notre Seigneur. \v 5 Par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, Dieu nous a donné la grâce et nous a envoyés comme apôtres. Nous sommes envoyés vers des gens de toutes les nations, pour qu’ils viennent à la foi et qu’ils obéissent à Dieu. Nous le faisons pour l’honneur de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. \v 6 Vous aussi, vous faites partie de ces gens. Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous a appelés à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenir. \v 7 Je vous écris donc, à vous tous qui êtes à Rome. Dieu vous aime et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a appelés à être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint. Que Dieu notre Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous donnent la grâce et la paix.

sw.L: Paulo, mtumwa wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, aliyeitwa [kuwa] mtume, aliyetengwa kwa ajili ya Injili ya Mungu, \v 2 ambayo aliiahidi tangu zamani kupitia manabii {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} katika Maandiko matakatifu, \v 3 kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, aliyetoka katika ukoo wa Daudi kwa kadiri ya mwili, \v 4 aliyewekwa kuwa Mwana wa Mungu katika nguvu kwa kadiri ya Roho wa utakatifu kutokana na ufufuo wa wafu, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Bwana wetu, \v 5 ambaye kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} tulipokea neema na utume kwa ajili ya utii wa imani katika mataifa yote kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 6 miongoni mwao ninyi pia mmo, mlioitwa [kuwa] wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 7 kwa wote walioko Roma, wapendwa wa Mungu, walioitwa [kuwa] watakatifu: neema kwenu na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Paulo, mtumishi wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, aliyeitwa kuwa mtume, akatengwa kwa ajili ya Injili ya Mungu. \v 2 Mungu aliiahidi Injili hii tangu zamani kupitia manabii {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} katika Maandiko Matakatifu. \v 3 Inamhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ambaye kwa ukoo wa kibinadamu alizaliwa katika uzao wa Daudi, \v 4 na ambaye aliwekwa kuwa Mwana wa Mungu mwenye nguvu, kupitia Roho wa utakatifu, kwa ufufuo wa wafu: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Bwana wetu. \v 5 Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} tumepokea neema na utume, ili kuleta utii wa imani katika mataifa yote kwa heshima ya jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. \v 6 Ninyi pia ni miongoni mwao, ninyi ambao Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amewaita muwe {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \v 7 Kwa ninyi nyote mlioko Roma, mnaopendwa na Mungu na mlioitwa kuwa watakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: neema na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ziwe nanyi.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Paulo. Mimi ni mtumishi wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Mungu aliniita niwe mtume, akanichagua nitangaze Habari Njema ya Mungu. \v 2 Zamani sana Mungu aliahidi Habari Njema hii kupitia manabii {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na ahadi hizo zimeandikwa katika Maandiko Matakatifu. \v 3 Habari Njema hii inamhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Kama mwanadamu, alizaliwa katika ukoo wa Mfalme Daudi. \v 4 Kupitia Roho Mtakatifu, Mungu alimweka kuwa Mwana wa Mungu mwenye nguvu alipomfufua kutoka kwa wafu. Yeye ni Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Bwana wetu. \v 5 Kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, Mungu ametupa neema na kututuma kama mitume. Ametutuma kwa watu wa mataifa yote, ili wamwamini Mungu na kumtii. Tunafanya hivi kwa heshima ya jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}. \v 6 Ninyi pia ni miongoni mwa watu hao. Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amewaita muwe watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \v 7 Kwa hiyo nawaandikia ninyi nyote mlioko Roma. Mungu anawapenda, na amewaita muwe watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walio watakatifu. Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wawape neema na amani.

decisions.reason: δοῦλος is a slave, a person owned by another. Paul calls himself the slave of Christ Jesus: he belongs to him entirely and acts at his command. The word also recalls the Old Testament title "servant of the LORD" given to Moses, David and the prophets, so it is a title of honor as well as of belonging.

ὁρίζω means to mark out, set or appoint (Acts 10:42 and 17:31 use it of Jesus appointed judge). Verse 3 already calls him God's Son, so the point is not that he became Son at the resurrection, but that by it he was installed as Son of God "in power": the risen Son now reigning. "Declared" is a common alternative, but the word is stronger than an announcement.

The phrase stands next to "Son of God" and contrasts with verse 3: born of David's line in weakness ("according to the flesh"), appointed Son of God in power. Read with the verb, it would only say how the appointing was done.

alternatives: Christ's own holy spirit or nature, set against his human nature ("flesh") in verse 3
decisions.reason: "Spirit of holiness" is a Hebrew way of saying "Holy Spirit" (Psalm 51:13 and Isaiah 63:10-11 have the same phrase in Hebrew). Verses 3-4 set "according to the flesh" against "according to the Spirit", as Paul does elsewhere (8:4-5, Galatians 4:29), and for Paul the Spirit is the one who raised Jesus (8:11). Some read it of Christ's own spirit, the holy nature that was his alongside his human descent. The levels follow the first reading.

decisions.choice: by the resurrection of the dead
decisions.reason: ἐξ can give the means ("by") or the starting point ("from the time of"); both make the resurrection the moment of the appointing. "The resurrection of the dead" is plural: Jesus' rising is the first of the resurrection God promised to the dead, not only his own return to life (1 Corinthians 15:20).

decisions.choice: "we" means Paul, possibly with the other apostles
decisions.reason: Romans is from Paul alone (1:1), and in verses 8-16 he says "I". The plural here is most likely his own grace and apostleship in a modest form, though it may include the other apostles. The translation keeps "we".

decisions.choice: grace and apostleship: the grace of being an apostle
alternatives: two separate gifts: grace (for salvation) and apostleship
decisions.reason: Paul often speaks of his calling as a grace given to him (12:3, 15:15-16), so the two words most likely name one gift. The levels keep both words and leave the relation open.

decisions.choice: the obedience that consists in faith and flows from it
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can be read several ways. Paul uses "obey" of believing the gospel (10:16) and also expects faith to issue in obedience (6:16-17). The phrase most likely holds both. The phrase comes again at 16:26.

ἔθνος means nations or peoples, and in Jewish use the nations other than Israel, the Gentiles. Paul was sent especially to the Gentiles (11:13, 15:16), and his readers in Rome are among them (verse 6). "All the nations" keeps the scope of his mission; verse 13 has the same word where the sense "Gentiles" is clearer.

decisions.choice: called to belong to Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: In Paul it is God who calls (8:30, 9:24), so "of Jesus Christ" says to whom they belong, not who called them.

decisions.choice: called to be holy ones, God's people
decisions.reason: ἅγιος is "holy", here as a noun: people set apart for God. It is what all believers are, not a few outstanding ones, as the Old Testament called Israel a holy people (Exodus 19:6).

alternatives: a few manuscripts leave out "in Rome" here and in verse 15
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts have "in Rome" in verses 7 and 15. A few, among them a Greek-Latin manuscript of the ninth century, leave it out, perhaps from copies made for general reading in the churches. The SBLGNT keeps it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

Letters of the time opened with "From A to B, greetings". Paul fills the greeting with grace and peace, the gift of God and the wholeness that follows from it (in Hebrew, shalom). His greeting here is the longest of his letters, because he has not yet visited Rome and introduces himself and his gospel.
Title setting.

decisions.choice: the greeting opens "From Paul" and ends its first sentence at verse 1
alternatives: one sentence to the end of verse 7
decisions.reason: The Greek greeting runs from verse 1 to verse 7 as one sentence. Balanced breaks it after each step of Paul's description so a listener can follow it, and opens with "From" so the first sentence reads as the sender of a letter, as Philippians 1:1 does.

decisions.choice: King David; for the honor of his name
decisions.reason: Readable adds "King" so a new reader knows who David is. "His name" is Jesus Christ's, who is named just before.

decisions.choice: {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}; {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish puts the article before "Mesías" but not before "Cristo", and "de el" contracts to "del", so the span takes in the preposition: "esclavo de Cristo Jesús" or "esclavo del Mesías Jesús". For "Jesus Christ" the default is the usual Spanish form of the name, "Jesucristo"; the alternative separates name and title, "Jesús, el Mesías".
Paul writes to the church in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Philippians.
"Siervo" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "esclavo".

"Gentiles" is the settled word where Paul means the non-Jewish peoples, and verse 13 uses it. Here the meaning decision keeps the scope of his mission, "all the nations", so Spanish says "naciones" at every level.

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}"; "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R); "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: the article stays outside the span ("du Christ" / "du Messie"), and "Jesus Christ" is written without the usual hyphen so that both options read naturally. French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for Paul's "in Christ" covers the preposition.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" and elided "l’" included (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs one the English lacks ("qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait promis", "à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenir"). Possessives agree with the noun ("{{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonne nouvelle"). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level ("nous avons reçu", "Dieu a promis") (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Romans is a letter: Paul speaks to his readers about what God has done and what has happened to him and to them, and French uses the passé composé for that. The plain past of a letter is not narrative, so the passé simple is not used, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: esclave (L), serviteur (B, R); l’Évangile (L, B), la bonne nouvelle (R); les saints (L), le peuple saint de Dieu (B, R) (for the whole book)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: The terms of the style guide, following the English levels: Literal keeps "esclave" for a slave's belonging to his master; "Évangile" with a capital is the message itself, which Readable says in plain words; "les saints" today suggests canonised individuals, so Balanced and Readable say that the readers are God's holy people.
"Mtumishi" in Balanced and Readable, as in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "mtumwa".

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake, lake, yeye)
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("aliiahidi", "alimweka", "alipomfufua"), and a prefix cannot take a capital. So the deity_pronoun setting applies only to the free pronouns and possessives, and Swahili has fewer spans than English. A pronoun at the start of a sentence ("Yeye ni Yesu") is capitalised anyway.

"Watu wa mataifa" is the settled phrase where Paul means the Gentiles, and verse 13 uses it. Here the meaning decision keeps the scope of his mission, "all the nations", so Swahili says "mataifa yote" at every level.
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.

records.literal_gloss: First indeed I thank the God of me through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because the faith of you is being proclaimed in whole the world.

en.L: First, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in the whole world.
en.B: To begin with, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} for every one of you, because people throughout the whole world are speaking of your faith.
en.R: First, I thank my God through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} for all of you. People all over the world are hearing about your faith.

es.L: Primero, doy gracias a mi Dios por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} por todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe se anuncia en todo el mundo.
es.B: Ante todo, doy gracias a mi Dios por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} por cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque la gente habla de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe por todo el mundo.
es.R: Lo primero: doy gracias a mi Dios por medio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} por todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Gente de todo el mundo está oyendo hablar de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe.

fr.L: Premièrement, je rends grâce à mon Dieu par Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pour vous tous, parce que votre foi est proclamée dans le monde entier.
fr.B: Tout d’abord, je remercie mon Dieu par Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} pour chacun de vous, car dans le monde entier on parle de votre foi.
fr.R: D’abord, je remercie mon Dieu par Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} pour vous tous. Partout dans le monde, les gens entendent parler de votre foi.

sw.L: Kwanza kabisa, ninamshukuru Mungu wangu kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuhusu ninyi nyote, kwa sababu imani yenu inatangazwa katika ulimwengu mzima.
sw.B: Kwa kuanzia, ninamshukuru Mungu wangu kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa ajili ya kila mmoja wenu, kwa sababu watu kote ulimwenguni wanazungumza habari za imani yenu.
sw.R: Kwanza, ninamshukuru Mungu wangu kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa ajili yenu nyote. Watu kila mahali duniani wanasikia habari za imani yenu.

decisions.reason: Πρῶτον μὲν usually begins a list, but Paul never reaches a "second". It means "to begin with": the first thing he does is give thanks.

decisions.choice: Paul's thanks reach God through Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Paul gives thanks through Jesus Christ, as he says all access to God comes through him (5:2, 7:25).
"In the whole world" is a natural way of saying "everywhere": the church in the capital was known among believers across the Roman world (16:19 says the same).
Title setting.

decisions.choice: people ... are speaking of / are hearing about your faith
decisions.reason: The passive "is being proclaimed" leaves out who proclaims it. Balanced and Readable name them as people, which is what the passive means.

source.text: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Witness for of me is the God, whom I serve in the spirit of me in the gospel of the Son of him, how unceasingly mention of you I make \v 10 always at the prayers of me, asking if somehow now at last I will be prospered in the will of the God to come to you.

en.L: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you, \v 10 always at my prayers asking if somehow now at last I may be given a good way, by the will of God, to come to you.
en.B: God, whom I serve with my whole spirit in proclaiming the gospel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, can testify how constantly I remember you \v 10 in my prayers. I am always asking that somehow, if God wills it, the way may at last be opened for me to come to you.
en.R: God knows that I am telling the truth. I serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all my heart by telling the good news about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. And God knows that I never stop praying for you. \v 10 Every time I pray, I ask God to make a way for me to come and visit you at last, if that is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

es.L: Porque testigo mío es Dios, a quien sirvo en mi espíritu en el evangelio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, de cómo sin cesar hago mención de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 10 siempre en mis oraciones pidiendo si de algún modo ya por fin se me abrirá un buen camino, por la voluntad de Dios, para ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Dios, a quien sirvo con todo mi espíritu anunciando el evangelio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, puede atestiguar cuán constantemente {{plural_you:los|os}} recuerdo \v 10 en mis oraciones. Siempre pido que de algún modo, si Dios lo quiere, por fin se me abra el camino para ir a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}.
es.R: Dios sabe que digo la verdad. Yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sirvo de todo corazón anunciando la buena noticia de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. Y Dios sabe que nunca dejo de orar por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 10 Cada vez que oro, pido a Dios que me abra el camino para ir a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} por fin, si eso es lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiere.

fr.L: Car Dieu m’est témoin, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je sers dans mon esprit dans l’Évangile de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, que sans cesse je fais mention de vous, \v 10 toujours dans mes prières, demandant si enfin, d’une manière ou d’une autre, il me sera accordé un heureux chemin, par la volonté de Dieu, pour venir vers vous.
fr.B: Dieu, que je sers de tout mon esprit en annonçant l’Évangile de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, peut témoigner que je me souviens de vous sans cesse \v 10 dans mes prières. Je demande toujours que, d’une manière ou d’une autre, si Dieu le veut, le chemin s’ouvre enfin devant moi pour que je vienne chez vous.
fr.R: Dieu sait que je dis la vérité. Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sers de tout mon cœur en annonçant la bonne nouvelle de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. Et Dieu sait que je prie sans cesse pour vous. \v 10 Chaque fois que je prie, je demande à Dieu de m’ouvrir un chemin pour que je puisse enfin venir vous voir, si c’est ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut.

sw.L: Kwa maana Mungu ni shahidi wangu, ambaye ninamtumikia katika roho yangu katika Injili ya Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, jinsi ninavyowataja bila kukoma, \v 10 siku zote katika maombi yangu nikiomba kama kwa njia yoyote sasa hatimaye nitapata njia njema, kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, ya kuja kwenu.
sw.B: Mungu, ninayemtumikia kwa roho yangu yote katika kuhubiri Injili ya Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, anaweza kushuhudia jinsi ninavyowakumbuka daima \v 10 katika maombi yangu. Siku zote ninaomba kwamba kwa namna fulani, Mungu akipenda, hatimaye njia ifunguke nije kwenu.
sw.R: Mungu anajua kwamba ninasema kweli. Ninamtumikia kwa moyo wangu wote kwa kuwaambia watu Habari Njema kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Mungu anajua pia kwamba siachi kuwaombea. \v 10 Kila ninapoomba, ninamwomba Mungu anifungulie njia nije kuwatembelea hatimaye, ikiwa ndivyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anavyotaka.

decisions.choice: an oath: God can confirm that this is true
decisions.reason: "God is my witness" calls on God to confirm what Paul says, as people swore by God in court. Paul uses it where readers who have not met him might doubt his words (2 Corinthians 1:23, Philippians 1:8).
λατρεύω is the word for serving God in worship, used of priests in the temple. Paul's preaching of the gospel is his worship (15:16 calls it priestly service).

decisions.choice: with my spirit: inwardly, with all of himself
decisions.reason: "My spirit" is Paul's own inner life, the opposite of outward ritual (as in 2:29). His service is whole-hearted and sincere, not only outward.

decisions.choice: be given a good way, succeed
decisions.reason: εὐοδόομαι once meant to have a good journey, but in Paul's time it meant to succeed or be helped along. Here the two meet: he prays for the way to Rome to open.

decisions.choice: God knows that I am telling the truth; with all my heart
alternatives: God is my witness; in my spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oath and "in my spirit" mean instead of reproducing them, since both are unfamiliar idioms.

The verb is service offered to God as worship, and Paul's service here is preaching the gospel. "Kumwabudu" (to worship) would leave out the work; "kumtumikia" (to serve) keeps it, and the meaning decision explains that this service is worship.

source.text: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς, τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I long for to see you, that some I may share gift with you spiritual for the to be strengthened you, \v 12 this and is to be encouraged together among you through the in one another faith of you both and of me.

en.L: For I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you, so that you may be strengthened, \v 12 that is, so that we may be encouraged together among you through each other's faith, both yours and mine.
en.B: I long to see you so that I can share some spiritual gift with you that will make you strong. \v 12 What I mean is that, while I am with you, we will be encouraged together by each other's faith, yours and mine.
en.R: I really want to see you. I want to give you some gift from the Spirit that will help you stand strong. \v 12 What I mean is that we can help each other. Your faith will encourage me, and my faith will encourage you.

es.L: Porque anhelo {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, para compartir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} algún don espiritual, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} fortalecidos, \v 12 es decir, para que seamos animados juntamente entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por medio de la fe de unos y otros, tanto {{plural_you:la de ustedes|la vuestra}} como la mía.
es.B: Deseo mucho {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} para compartir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} algún don espiritual que {{plural_you:les|os}} dé firmeza. \v 12 Quiero decir que, estando con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, seremos animados juntos por la fe de unos y otros, {{plural_you:la de ustedes|la vuestra}} y la mía.
es.R: De verdad quiero {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}. Quiero {{plural_you:darles|daros}} algún don del Espíritu que {{plural_you:les|os}} ayude a {{plural_you:mantenerse|manteneros}} firmes. \v 12 Lo que quiero decir es que podemos ayudarnos unos a otros. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} fe me animará a mí, y mi fe {{plural_you:los|os}} animará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Car je désire vivement vous voir, afin de vous communiquer quelque don spirituel, pour que vous soyez affermis, \v 12 c’est-à-dire pour être encouragés ensemble au milieu de vous par notre foi mutuelle, la vôtre et la mienne.
fr.B: J’ai un vif désir de vous voir, pour partager avec vous quelque don spirituel qui vous rendra forts. \v 12 Je veux dire que, lorsque je serai parmi vous, nous serons encouragés ensemble par la foi les uns des autres, la vôtre et la mienne.
fr.R: J’ai vraiment envie de vous voir. Je veux vous donner un don qui vient de l’Esprit et qui vous aidera à rester forts. \v 12 Je veux dire par là que nous pourrons nous aider les uns les autres. Votre foi m’encouragera, et ma foi vous encouragera.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninatamani kuwaona, ili niwashirikishe karama fulani ya kiroho, ili mpate kuimarishwa, \v 12 yaani, ili tutiwe moyo pamoja kati yenu kupitia imani tuliyo nayo sisi kwa sisi, yenu na yangu.
sw.B: Ninatamani kuwaona ili niwagawie karama fulani ya kiroho itakayowaimarisha. \v 12 Ninamaanisha kwamba, nikiwa pamoja nanyi, sote tutatiwa moyo kwa imani ya kila mmoja wetu, imani yenu na yangu.
sw.R: Ninataka sana kuwaona. Nataka niwape zawadi fulani kutoka kwa Roho itakayowasaidia kusimama imara. \v 12 Ninachomaanisha ni kwamba tunaweza kusaidiana. Imani yenu itanitia moyo mimi, na imani yangu itawatia moyo ninyi.

decisions.choice: a gift that comes from the Spirit
alternatives: a particular gift such as teaching
decisions.reason: χάρισμα is a gift of grace. With "spiritual" it is a gift the Spirit gives for building others up, as in 12:6 and 1 Corinthians 12. Paul does not say which gift he has in mind.
The verb is passive. Paul gives the gift, but the strength is God's work (16:25 says God is able to strengthen them).

decisions.choice: Paul clarifies: the help goes both ways
decisions.reason: "That is" restates what he has just said. Writing to a church he did not found, he adds at once that he will receive from them as much as he gives.

decisions.choice: a gift from the Spirit; Your faith will encourage me, and my faith will encourage you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "spiritual" means here and spells out "each other's faith" in two plain clauses.

source.text: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not I want and you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I purposed to come to you, and was prevented until the present, that some fruit I might have also among you as also among the other nations.

en.L: Now I do not want you to be unaware, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that many times I planned to come to you, and was prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as also among the rest of the Gentiles.
en.B: I want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that I have often planned to come to you, so that I might gather some harvest among you too, as I have among the other Gentiles, but until now I have been kept from coming.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I want you to know that many times I have planned to visit you. But each time, something has kept me from coming. I want to see my work bear fruit among you, as it has among other non-Jewish people.

es.L: Ahora bien, no quiero que {{plural_you:ignoren|ignoréis}}, hermanos, que muchas veces me propuse ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y he sido impedido hasta ahora, para tener algún fruto también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, así como también entre los demás gentiles.
es.B: Quiero que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}}, hermanos, que muchas veces he planeado ir a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, para recoger alguna cosecha también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como ya ha sucedido entre los demás gentiles; pero hasta ahora se me ha impedido.
es.R: Hermanos, quiero que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que muchas veces he planeado {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}. Pero cada vez algo me ha impedido ir. Quiero ver que mi trabajo dé fruto entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como lo ha dado entre otros que no son judíos.

fr.L: Or je ne veux pas que vous ignoriez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, que souvent je me suis proposé de venir vers vous, et j’en ai été empêché jusqu’à présent, afin d’avoir quelque fruit parmi vous aussi, comme aussi parmi les autres nations.
fr.B: Je veux que vous le sachiez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : j’ai souvent formé le projet de venir chez vous, afin de recueillir quelque fruit parmi vous aussi, comme parmi les autres non-Juifs, mais jusqu’à présent j’en ai été empêché.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je veux que vous le sachiez : bien des fois, j’ai eu le projet de venir vous voir. Mais chaque fois, quelque chose m’en a empêché. Je voudrais que mon travail porte du fruit chez vous, comme il en a porté chez les autres non-Juifs.

sw.L: Basi sitaki mkose kufahamu, ndugu, kwamba mara nyingi nilipanga kuja kwenu, na nimezuiwa mpaka sasa, ili nipate tunda fulani kwenu pia, kama ilivyo pia kati ya watu wa mataifa waliobaki.
sw.B: Ndugu, nataka mjue kwamba mara nyingi nimepanga kuja kwenu, ili nipate mavuno fulani kati yenu pia, kama nilivyopata kati ya watu wa mataifa wengine; lakini hadi sasa nimezuiwa.
sw.R: Ndugu, nataka mjue kwamba mara nyingi nimepanga kuwatembelea. Lakini kila mara kitu fulani kimenizuia nisije. Nataka kuona kazi yangu ikizaa matunda kati yenu, kama ilivyozaa kati ya watu wengine wasio Wayahudi.

decisions.reason: "I do not want you to be unaware" is Paul's way of introducing something important (11:25, 1 Corinthians 10:1). It says the opposite in negative form, and means a firm "I want you to know".

decisions.choice: Paul was prevented; he does not say by whom
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the cause unnamed. In 15:22 he explains that his work in the eastern provinces kept him from coming.

decisions.choice: fruit: the results of his work
decisions.reason: The fruit is what Paul's ministry produces: people coming to faith and growing in it, as in Philippians 1:22.
The same word as "nations" in verse 5. With "the rest" it means the other non-Jewish peoples Paul has worked among, and it shows that he counts the believers in Rome among the Gentiles.
Paul writes to the whole church, women and men (16:1-15 greets many women by name). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: the parenthesis "and was prevented until now" moves to the end
decisions.reason: In the Greek the clause about being prevented interrupts the sentence. Balanced moves it to the end so the purpose clause follows the plan it belongs to.
"Gentiles" is church language; Readable says what it means.

As in Philippians 4:1, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so adding "y hermanas" would add words the Greek does not have, and there is no gender span. For review: Romans 16 greets many women by name, and a reviewer may prefer to make the women explicit.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English, Paul addresses the whole church, women and men; "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Words that agree with the noun need no span.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B, R) where the English says "Gentiles"; les nations where it says "nations" (1:5) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Les Gentils" is no longer current French and "les païens" sounds pejorative today. Literal keeps the biblical "les nations"; Balanced and Readable say plainly that the peoples other than Israel are meant.

alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span here; the only traditional alternative would add "wa kiume" (male) and change the meaning.

source.text: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·

records.literal_gloss: To Greeks both and to barbarians, to wise both and to foolish debtor I am;

en.L: Both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to [the] wise and to [the] foolish, I am a debtor;
en.B: I am under obligation to Greeks and to non-Greeks, to the educated and to the uneducated.
en.R: I have a duty to everyone: to people who speak Greek and to those who do not, to the educated and to the uneducated.

es.L: Tanto a griegos como a bárbaros, tanto a sabios como a necios, soy deudor;
es.B: Tengo una obligación con los griegos y con los que no son griegos, con la gente culta y con la que no tiene estudios.
es.R: Tengo un deber con todos: con los que hablan griego y con los que no, con los que han estudiado y con los que no.

fr.L: Aux Grecs comme aux barbares, aux sages comme aux insensés, je suis débiteur ;
fr.B: J’ai une dette envers les Grecs et les non-Grecs, envers les gens instruits et ceux qui ne le sont pas.
fr.R: J’ai un devoir envers tout le monde : envers ceux qui parlent grec et ceux qui ne le parlent pas, envers les gens instruits et les gens sans instruction.

sw.L: Kwa Wagiriki na kwa wasio Wagiriki, kwa wenye hekima na kwa wajinga, mimi ni mdaiwa;
sw.B: Nina wajibu kwa Wagiriki na kwa wasio Wagiriki, kwa wasomi na kwa wasiosoma.
sw.R: Nina wajibu kwa watu wote: kwa watu wanaozungumza Kigiriki na kwa wasiozungumza, kwa waliosoma na kwa wasiosoma.

decisions.reason: Greek speakers called everyone who did not speak Greek "barbarians", from the sound of a foreign language. The word meant foreigners, not savages. With "Greeks" it covers every people in the empire and beyond it, such as the Spain Paul hopes to reach (15:24).

alternatives: the wise and the foolish (in a moral sense)
decisions.reason: The second pair matches the first: cultured, educated people and simple, unlearned ones. It is about education, not about goodness or folly before God.

alternatives: owing them a debt (something taken from them)
decisions.reason: ὀφειλέτης is a debtor. Paul owes the gospel to all these people: he has received it, and God has given him the task of passing it on (1 Corinthians 9:16).
In English "barbarians" means cruel or uncivilized people, which the Greek word did not. Literal keeps "barbarians" to show the form.

decisions.choice: I have a duty to everyone
decisions.reason: Readable names what the two pairs add up to before listing them.

"Washenzi" means savage or uncivilized people and is an insult, which the Greek word was not; it meant those who do not speak Greek. Swahili says that at Literal as well, unlike the English Literal, because no Swahili word keeps the form without the insult.

source.text: οὕτως τὸ κατ’ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: So the as to me eager [is] also to you the [ones] in Rome to proclaim the gospel.

en.L: So, as far as it rests with me, [I am] eager to proclaim the gospel to you also who are in Rome.
en.B: So, for my part, I am eager to bring the gospel to you in Rome as well.
en.R: That is why I want so much to tell the good news to you in Rome too.

es.L: Así, por lo que de mí depende, [estoy] deseoso de anunciar el evangelio también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en Roma.
es.B: Por eso, por mi parte, estoy deseoso de llevar el evangelio también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los de Roma.
es.R: Por eso deseo tanto anunciar la buena noticia también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} en Roma.

fr.L: Ainsi, pour ce qui dépend de moi, [je suis] plein d’ardeur pour vous annoncer l’Évangile, à vous aussi qui êtes à Rome.
fr.B: Ainsi, pour ma part, je suis impatient de vous porter l’Évangile, à vous aussi qui êtes à Rome.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi je désire tant vous annoncer la bonne nouvelle, à vous aussi qui êtes à Rome.

sw.L: Hivyo, kwa kadiri inavyonihusu, [nina] shauku ya kuwatangazia Injili ninyi pia mlioko Roma.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, mimi binafsi nina shauku ya kuwaletea Injili ninyi pia mlioko Roma.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu ninatamani sana kuwaambia Habari Njema ninyi pia mlioko Roma.

decisions.choice: for my part, I am eager
decisions.reason: The phrase is a noun, "the eagerness as far as concerns me". Paul is ready; whether he comes depends on God (verse 10).

The Romans already believe (verse 8), yet Paul wants to proclaim the gospel to them. For him the gospel is not only the first message but what believers go on living by, and the letter itself sets it out for them.

alternatives: a few manuscripts leave it out
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, a few manuscripts leave out "in Rome". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: bring the gospel / tell the good news
decisions.reason: The verb is the one formed from the word gospel: to announce good news. "Preach" suggests a sermon, so Balanced says "bring the gospel" and Readable "tell the good news".

decisions.choice: annoncer l’Évangile (L), porter l’Évangile (B), annoncer la bonne nouvelle (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for the gospel. "Évangéliser" today suggests mission to unbelievers, and "prêcher" a sermon; the readers are already believers (m2), so French says that the good news is brought or announced to them.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·

records.literal_gloss: Not for I am ashamed of the gospel, power for of God it is for salvation to everyone the believing, to Jew both first and to Greek;

en.L: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, both to [the] Jew first and to [the] Greek;
en.B: I am not ashamed of the gospel. It is God's own power at work to save everyone who believes, the Jew first and the Greek as well.
en.R: I am not ashamed of the good news. It is God's power to save everyone who believes. It is for the Jews first, and also for people who are not Jews.

es.L: Porque no me avergüenzo del evangelio, porque es poder de Dios para salvación de todo el que cree, tanto del judío primero como del griego;
es.B: No me avergüenzo del evangelio. Es el poder mismo de Dios en acción para salvar a todo el que cree, al judío primero y también al griego.
es.R: No me da vergüenza la buena noticia. Es el poder de Dios para salvar a todos los que creen. Es primero para los judíos, y también para los que no son judíos.

fr.L: Car je n’ai pas honte de l’Évangile : il est en effet puissance de Dieu en vue du salut pour chacun de ceux qui croient, pour le Juif d’abord comme pour le Grec ;
fr.B: Je n’ai pas honte de l’Évangile. C’est la puissance même de Dieu à l’œuvre pour sauver tous ceux qui croient, le Juif d’abord, et le Grec aussi.
fr.R: Je n’ai pas honte de la bonne nouvelle. C’est la puissance de Dieu pour sauver tous ceux qui croient. Elle est d’abord pour les Juifs, et aussi pour ceux qui ne sont pas juifs.

sw.L: Kwa maana siionei aibu Injili, kwa maana ni nguvu ya Mungu kwa ajili ya wokovu kwa kila mtu aaminiye, kwa Myahudi kwanza na pia kwa Mgiriki;
sw.B: Siionei aibu Injili. Ni nguvu ya Mungu ikifanya kazi ili kuokoa kila mtu anayeamini, Myahudi kwanza na Mgiriki pia.
sw.R: Sioni aibu kuhusu Habari Njema. Ni nguvu ya Mungu ya kuokoa kila mtu anayeamini. Ni kwa ajili ya Wayahudi kwanza, na pia kwa ajili ya watu wasio Wayahudi.

decisions.choice: not ashamed: confident in it, ready to stand by it
decisions.reason: A message about a crucified man was foolishness to many (1 Corinthians 1:23). "Not ashamed" says, by denying the opposite, that Paul stands openly by it, as Jesus speaks of being ashamed of him and his words (Mark 8:38).
The gospel does not only describe God's power: when it is proclaimed and believed, God's power is at work in it to save (1 Corinthians 1:18).

decisions.choice: Greek: anyone who is not a Jew
decisions.reason: Paired with "Jew", "Greek" stands for all non-Jews, Romans included, as in 2:9-10 and 10:12.

decisions.choice: first: Israel's priority in God's plan
decisions.reason: The gospel came first to the Jews, to whom the promises were given (verse 2, 3:2, 9:4-5), and Paul's own mission began in the synagogues. "First" keeps that order, while "everyone who believes" makes the gospel equally for both.
Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, which English uses more naturally; "save" is one of the key term's settled words.
Readable says what "Greek" means here.

source.text: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Righteousness for of God in it is revealed from faith to faith, as it has been written: The and righteous from faith will live.

en.L: For in it [the] righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, just as it is written: "But the righteous [one] will live by faith."
en.B: In it the righteousness of God is being revealed, from faith for faith. As it is written, "The one who is righteous will live by faith."
en.R: The good news shows God's righteousness: how God puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}. It comes by faith, and it leads to faith. As Scripture says, "The person who is righteous will live by faith."

es.L: Porque en él [la] justicia de Dios se revela de fe a fe, así como está escrito: «Pero el justo vivirá por [la] fe».
es.B: En él se está revelando la justicia de Dios, de fe para fe. Como está escrito: «El que es justo vivirá por la fe».
es.R: La buena noticia muestra la justicia de Dios: cómo Dios pone a las personas en una relación correcta con {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}}. Esa justicia viene por la fe y lleva a la fe. Como dice la Escritura: «La persona que es justa vivirá por la fe».

fr.L: Car en lui la justice de Dieu est révélée, de la foi vers la foi, selon qu’il est écrit : « Or le juste vivra par la foi. »
fr.B: C’est en lui que la justice de Dieu se révèle, de la foi vers la foi, comme il est écrit : « Celui qui est juste vivra par la foi. »
fr.R: La bonne nouvelle montre la justice de Dieu : comment Dieu met les gens en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Cela vient par la foi, et cela conduit à la foi. Comme le dit l’Écriture : « Celui qui est juste vivra par la foi. »

sw.L: Kwa maana ndani yake haki ya Mungu inafunuliwa kutoka katika imani kuelekea imani, kama ilivyoandikwa: "Lakini mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani."
sw.B: Ndani ya Injili haki ya Mungu inafunuliwa, kutoka imani kwa ajili ya imani. Kama ilivyoandikwa, "Mtu aliye mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani."
sw.R: Habari Njema inaonyesha haki ya Mungu: jinsi Mungu anavyowaweka watu katika uhusiano mwema naye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Haki hiyo inakuja kwa imani, na inaongoza kwenye imani. Kama Maandiko yasemavyo, "Mtu aliye mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani."

decisions.choice: God's righteousness: God acting rightly to put people right with himself
alternatives: a righteousness that God gives to people (a status from God)
God's own justice or faithfulness, as a quality of God
decisions.reason: In the Psalms and Isaiah, God's righteousness is God acting faithfully to save and set right (Psalm 98:2, Isaiah 46:13, 51:5-8). Romans speaks of it as God's own (3:5, 3:25-26) and also as given to those who believe (3:22, 5:17). The phrase most likely holds both: God shows himself right by putting people right.

decisions.choice: from faith for faith: from start to finish it is by faith
alternatives: from God's faithfulness to human faith
from the faith of one believer to another
from Old Testament faith to New Testament faith
decisions.reason: The phrase gives a starting point and a goal, and both are faith. Paul most likely means that faith is how righteousness is received and where it leads, with nothing else added (as 3:22 says "through faith ... for all who believe"). Other readings take the first "faith" as God's faithfulness.

The quotation is from Habakkuk 2:4. The Hebrew says "the righteous will live by his faithfulness"; most copies of the old Greek translation (the Septuagint) say "by my faithfulness", meaning God's. Paul leaves out the pronoun. He uses the verse again in Galatians 3:11.

alternatives: "by faith" goes with "the righteous": "the one who is righteous by faith will live"
decisions.reason: The Greek order, "the righteous by faith will live", allows both. In Habakkuk the phrase goes with "live", and that reading is followed here. Paul's argument from 1:17 to chapter 5 stresses righteousness by faith and then life (5:1, 5:17-18), so the other reading also fits.

decisions.choice: how God puts people right with himself
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the righteousness of God" as the meaning decision describes it; reviewers should check that it does not narrow the phrase.

decisions.choice: As it is written / As Scripture says
alternatives: just as it has been written
decisions.reason: "It is written" is the normal formula for quoting Scripture; Readable names Scripture.

decisions.choice: la justice de Dieu; juste, at every level, with Readable explaining it as God putting people "en règle avec lui" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "La justice" is the French word that keeps the link between God's righteousness, the righteous person and "justifier" (L) / "déclarer juste" (B). It can suggest a court's punishment, so Readable adds what the meaning decision describes (m1): God acting to put people right with himself.

source.text: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων, διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.

records.literal_gloss: Is revealed for wrath of God from heaven upon all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people the [ones] the truth in unrighteousness holding down, \v 19 because the known of the God plain is among them, the God for to them made [it] plain.

en.L: For [the] wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of {{gender:people|men}} who suppress the truth by unrighteousness, \v 19 because what can be known about God is plain among them, for God made [it] plain to them.
en.B: God's wrath is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wrongdoing of {{gender:people|men}} who by their wrongdoing hold down the truth. \v 19 For what can be known about God is plain to them, because God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has made it plain to them.
en.R: From heaven, God is showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger against people who do not honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and who do what is wrong. By doing wrong, they push the truth away. \v 19 But they can know the truth about God, because God has made it clear to them.

es.L: Porque [la] ira de Dios se revela desde [el] cielo contra toda impiedad e injusticia de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} que suprimen la verdad mediante la injusticia, \v 19 porque lo que se puede conocer de Dios es evidente entre ellos, pues Dios se [lo] hizo evidente.
es.B: La ira de Dios se está revelando desde el cielo contra toda la impiedad y la injusticia de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}} que, con su injusticia, sofocan la verdad. \v 19 Pues lo que se puede conocer de Dios está claro para ellos, porque Dios mismo se lo ha mostrado con claridad.
es.R: Desde el cielo, Dios está mostrando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira contra la gente que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} honra y que actúa con injusticia. Con su injusticia, apartan la verdad. \v 19 Pero pueden conocer la verdad acerca de Dios, porque Dios se la ha mostrado claramente.

fr.L: Car la colère de Dieu est révélée du ciel contre toute impiété et injustice des {{gender:humains|hommes}} qui étouffent la vérité par l’injustice, \v 19 parce que ce qu’on peut connaître de Dieu est manifeste parmi eux, car Dieu [le] leur a manifesté.
fr.B: La colère de Dieu se révèle du haut du ciel contre toute l’impiété et tout le mal des {{gender:humains|hommes}} qui, par le mal qu’ils font, étouffent la vérité. \v 19 Car ce qu’on peut connaître de Dieu leur est évident : Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} le leur a rendu évident.
fr.R: Du haut du ciel, Dieu montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère contre les gens qui ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}honorent pas et qui font le mal. En faisant le mal, ils repoussent la vérité. \v 19 Pourtant, ils peuvent connaître la vérité sur Dieu, car Dieu la leur a montrée clairement.

sw.L: Kwa maana ghadhabu ya Mungu inafunuliwa kutoka mbinguni dhidi ya kila namna ya kutomcha Mungu na kutokuwa na haki kwa wanadamu wanaoizuia kweli kwa kutokuwa na haki, \v 19 kwa sababu kile kinachoweza kujulikana kuhusu Mungu kiko wazi kati yao, kwa maana Mungu alikiweka wazi kwao.
sw.B: Ghadhabu ya Mungu inafunuliwa kutoka mbinguni dhidi ya kutomcha Mungu kote na udhalimu wote wa wanadamu wanaoikandamiza kweli kwa udhalimu wao. \v 19 Kwa maana kile kinachoweza kujulikana kuhusu Mungu kiko wazi kwao, kwa sababu Mungu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} amekiweka wazi kwao.
sw.R: Kutoka mbinguni, Mungu anaonyesha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} dhidi ya watu wasiomheshimu na wanaotenda mabaya. Kwa matendo yao mabaya wanaisukuma kweli mbali. \v 19 Lakini wanaweza kujua kweli kuhusu Mungu, kwa sababu Mungu amewaonyesha waziwazi.

decisions.choice: God's wrath: his settled opposition to evil and his judgment on it
decisions.reason: ὀργή is anger. God's wrath in Paul is not a fit of temper but his just response to evil, carried out in judgment (2:5-8). The next verses show it at work already: God hands people over to what they have chosen (verses 24, 26, 28).

alternatives: will be revealed at the judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is present, as in verse 17: God's righteousness and his wrath are both being revealed now. Paul also speaks of a coming day of wrath (2:5).

ἀσέβεια is failure to honor God; ἀδικία is wrongdoing, the lack of righteousness. The second word is formed from the same root as "righteousness" in verse 17: God's righteousness is revealed, and so is his wrath against human unrighteousness.
κατέχω can mean to hold fast or to hold back. Here it is to hold the truth down so that it does not act or speak.
"In them" can mean within each person or among people. Verse 20 says God is known through what he made, so the knowledge is open to all, and the translation leaves both open.
Balanced and Readable use plain words for ἀδικία. Literal keeps "unrighteousness" so that the link with "righteousness" in verse 17 stays visible.
"Wrath" is rare in everyday English; Readable says "anger".
The word means human beings, men and women.

English Balanced and Readable use plain words for "unrighteousness" and lose its link with "righteousness" in verse 17. In Spanish "injusticia" is both the plain word and the opposite of "justicia", so every level keeps it and the link stays visible.
Unlike English "wrath", Spanish "ira" is an everyday word, so Readable keeps the key term.

decisions.choice: {{gender:humains|hommes}} (for the whole book, where the word means human beings)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women. French "les hommes" is read as men less and less, so the inclusive "les humains" is the default and the traditional form the alternative; Readable already says "les gens" and needs no span.
English Readable changes "wrath" to "anger" because "wrath" is rare; French "colère" is already the everyday word, so all three levels keep it.
"Ghadhabu" is well known and is the settled word for God's wrath, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "anger". "Hasira" is ordinary human anger.

source.text: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους, διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·

records.literal_gloss: The for invisible [things] of him from creation of world by the made [things] being understood are clearly seen, the both eternal of him power and divinity, for the to be them without excuse, \v 21 because having known the God not as God they glorified or gave thanks, but they became futile in the reasonings of them and was darkened the senseless of them heart;

en.L: For since [the] creation of [the] world {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} invisible [attributes] are clearly seen, being understood through the things made, both {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eternal power and divine nature, so that they are without excuse, \v 21 because, although they knew God, they did not glorify [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened;
en.B: Since the world was made, what cannot be seen of God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} everlasting power and divine nature, has been in plain view, understood from the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made. So they have no excuse. \v 21 Although they knew God, they did not give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory as God or thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their reasoning turned to emptiness, and darkness filled their senseless hearts.
en.R: No one can see God. But since the beginning of the world, people have been able to understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is like from the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made. They can see that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power lasts forever and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is truly God. So people have no excuse. \v 21 They knew God, but they did not give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the glory {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserves as God, and they did not thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their thinking became worthless, and their foolish minds were filled with darkness.

es.L: Porque desde [la] creación del mundo {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} [atributos] invisibles se ven claramente, siendo entendidos por medio de las cosas hechas, tanto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} eterno poder como [{{deity_pronoun:su|Su}}] naturaleza divina, de modo que ellos quedan sin excusa, \v 21 porque, aunque conocieron a Dios, no [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] glorificaron como Dios ni [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] dieron gracias, sino que se volvieron vanos en sus razonamientos, y su insensato corazón fue oscurecido;
es.B: Desde que el mundo fue creado, lo que no se puede ver de Dios, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder sempiterno y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} naturaleza divina, ha estado a la vista, y se entiende por las cosas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo. Así que no tienen excusa. \v 21 Aunque conocieron a Dios, no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron gloria como a Dios ni {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron gracias. Sus razonamientos se volvieron vacíos, y la oscuridad llenó sus corazones sin entendimiento.
es.R: Nadie puede ver a Dios. Pero desde el principio del mundo, la gente ha podido entender cómo es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por las cosas que ha hecho. Pueden ver que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder dura para siempre y que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es de verdad Dios. Así que la gente no tiene excusa. \v 21 Conocían a Dios, pero no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron la gloria que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} merece como Dios, ni {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dieron gracias. Su manera de pensar se volvió inútil, y sus mentes necias se llenaron de oscuridad.

fr.L: Car depuis la création du monde, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} [qualités] invisibles se voient clairement, comprises par les choses faites, à la fois {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance éternelle et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} divinité, de sorte qu’ils sont sans excuse, \v 21 parce que, ayant connu Dieu, ils ne [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]ont pas glorifié comme Dieu et ne [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] ont pas rendu grâce, mais ils sont devenus vains dans leurs raisonnements, et leur cœur sans intelligence a été obscurci ;
fr.B: Depuis la création du monde, ce qu’on ne peut voir de Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance qui n’a pas de fin et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} nature divine, est bien visible : on le comprend par les choses qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faites. Ils n’ont donc aucune excuse. \v 21 Bien qu’ils aient connu Dieu, ils ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont pas rendu gloire comme à Dieu et ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas remercié. Leurs raisonnements sont devenus vides, et les ténèbres ont envahi leur cœur insensé.
fr.R: Personne ne peut voir Dieu. Mais depuis le commencement du monde, les gens peuvent comprendre à quoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressemble en regardant ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait. Ils peuvent voir que {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance dure toujours et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vraiment Dieu. Les gens n’ont donc aucune excuse. \v 21 Ils connaissaient Dieu, mais ils ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont pas rendu la gloire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mérite comme Dieu, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont pas remercié. Leurs pensées sont devenues sans valeur, et les ténèbres ont rempli leur esprit sans intelligence.

sw.L: Kwa maana tangu kuumbwa kwa ulimwengu [sifa] {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zisizoonekana zinaonekana wazi, zikitambulika kupitia vitu vilivyofanywa, yaani nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} za milele na hali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya uungu, ili wao wasiwe na cha kujitetea, \v 21 kwa sababu, ingawa walimjua Mungu, hawakumtukuza kama Mungu wala hawakumshukuru, bali wakawa bure katika hoja zao, na moyo wao usio na akili ukafunikwa na giza;
sw.B: Tangu ulimwengu ulipoumbwa, yale ambayo hayaonekani kuhusu Mungu, yaani nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zisizo na mwisho na hali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya uungu, yamekuwa wazi mbele ya macho, yakieleweka kupitia vitu alivyoviumba. Kwa hiyo hawana cha kujitetea. \v 21 Ingawa walimjua Mungu, hawakumpa utukufu kama Mungu wala hawakumshukuru. Hoja zao zikageuka kuwa ubatili, na mioyo yao isiyo na ufahamu ikajaa giza.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kumwona Mungu. Lakini tangu mwanzo wa ulimwengu, watu wameweza kuelewa jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyo kupitia vitu alivyovifanya. Wanaweza kuona kwamba nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zinadumu milele na kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni Mungu kweli. Kwa hiyo watu hawana udhuru. \v 21 Walimjua Mungu, lakini hawakumpa utukufu anaoustahili kama Mungu, wala hawakumshukuru. Mawazo yao yakawa hayana faida, na akili zao za kipumbavu zikajaa giza.

decisions.reason: Paul sets the two words side by side on purpose: God, who cannot be seen, is clearly seen by the mind ("being understood") in what he has made.
θειότης is the quality of being divine. Creation shows that its maker is God and has eternal power; it does not show everything about God.

decisions.choice: so that they are without excuse: the result
alternatives: in order that they might be without excuse: God's purpose
decisions.reason: The construction can give purpose or result. The point is the outcome, that no one can plead ignorance, not that God revealed himself in order to condemn.
The participle grants a fact against which the rest stands out: they knew him, yet did not honor him.
ματαιόομαι is to become empty or worthless. The Old Testament calls idols "empty things" and says their makers become like them (Jeremiah 2:5, Psalm 115:8).

decisions.choice: heart: the center of thought and will
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where a person thinks and decides, not only where they feel. A darkened heart is a mind that no longer sees.
Balanced and Readable use the noun, which is plainer English; the key term allows "glory" for this verb.
In English "heart" suggests feelings; Readable says "minds", as the meaning decision explains.
The word here is not the one Open Word Bible renders "eternal" (as in "eternal life"); "everlasting" keeps them apart.

source.text: φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν, καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Claiming to be wise they became foolish, \v 23 and they exchanged the glory of the immortal God in likeness of image of mortal human and of birds and of four-footed [animals] and of creeping [things].

en.L: Claiming to be wise, they became fools, \v 23 and they exchanged the glory of the immortal God for a likeness of an image of {{gender:a mortal human|mortal man}} and of birds and of four-footed [animals] and of creeping things.
en.B: They claimed to be wise, but they became fools. \v 23 They traded the glory of the God who never dies for images made to look like mortal human beings, or birds, or beasts, or creatures that crawl.
en.R: They said they were wise, but they became foolish. \v 23 God is glorious and lives forever. But they stopped worshiping {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and worshiped idols instead. They made idols that looked like people, who die, and like birds, animals and creatures that crawl.

es.L: Afirmando que eran sabios, se volvieron insensatos, \v 23 y trocaron la gloria del Dios inmortal por la semejanza de una imagen de {{gender:un ser humano mortal|un hombre mortal}}, y de aves, y de cuadrúpedos, y de [seres] que se arrastran.
es.B: Decían ser sabios, pero se volvieron necios. \v 23 Cambiaron la gloria del Dios que nunca muere por imágenes hechas con la forma de seres humanos mortales, o de aves, o de bestias, o de animales que se arrastran.
es.R: Decían que eran sabios, pero se volvieron tontos. \v 23 Dios es glorioso y vive para siempre. Pero dejaron de adorar a Dios y adoraron ídolos en lugar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Hicieron ídolos con forma de personas, que mueren, y de aves, animales y criaturas que se arrastran.

fr.L: Prétendant être sages, ils sont devenus fous, \v 23 et ils ont échangé la gloire du Dieu immortel contre une ressemblance d’image d’un {{gender:être humain|homme}} mortel, et d’oiseaux, et de quadrupèdes, et de bêtes rampantes.
fr.B: Ils prétendaient être sages, mais ils sont devenus fous. \v 23 Ils ont troqué la gloire du Dieu qui ne meurt jamais contre des images faites à la ressemblance d’êtres humains mortels, d’oiseaux, de bêtes à quatre pattes ou de créatures qui rampent.
fr.R: Ils disaient qu’ils étaient sages, mais ils sont devenus fous. \v 23 Dieu est glorieux et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit pour toujours. Mais ils ont cessé de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorer et ils ont adoré des idoles à la place. Ils ont fabriqué des idoles qui ressemblaient à des humains, qui meurent, et à des oiseaux, à des animaux et à des bêtes qui rampent.

sw.L: Wakisema kwamba wao ni wenye hekima, wakawa wajinga, \v 23 nao wakaubadilisha utukufu wa Mungu asiyekufa kwa mfano wa sanamu ya mwanadamu anayekufa, na ya ndege, na ya viumbe vya miguu minne, na ya vitu vinavyotambaa.
sw.B: Walijidai kuwa na hekima, lakini wakawa wapumbavu. \v 23 Walibadilisha utukufu wa Mungu asiyekufa kwa sanamu zilizotengenezwa kufanana na wanadamu wanaokufa, au ndege, au wanyama, au viumbe vinavyotambaa.
sw.R: Walisema wana hekima, lakini wakawa wapumbavu. \v 23 Mungu ni mwenye utukufu na anaishi milele. Lakini waliacha kumwabudu, wakaabudu sanamu badala {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Walitengeneza sanamu zinazofanana na watu, ambao hufa, na ndege, wanyama na viumbe vinavyotambaa.

decisions.reason: Psalm 106:20 says Israel at the golden calf "exchanged their glory for the image of an ox", and Jeremiah 2:11 says God's people "exchanged their glory" for what does not help. Deuteronomy 4:16-18 forbids images of men or women, animals, birds and creeping things. Paul tells the story of all humanity in Israel's words.
Human beings, birds, four-footed animals and creeping things are the creatures of Genesis 1:20-26. People worshiped the creatures they were made to rule over.

decisions.choice: a likeness of an image: a copy of a copy
decisions.reason: Paul doubles the words: they worshiped not even creatures but a likeness of their image, an idol shaped like them.
ἄφθαρτος is "not subject to decay", φθαρτός "subject to decay": the God who never dies against human beings who die.

decisions.choice: they stopped worshiping him and worshiped idols instead
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "exchanged the glory of God for a likeness of an image" describes: the worship of idols.
The word means a human being. Balanced and Readable already use inclusive words and need no setting.

The Greek words mean "not subject to decay" and "subject to decay", as the meaning decision explains. Said of God and of people, "asiyeharibika" would sound like a thing that does not spoil; "asiyekufa" (who does not die) and "anayekufa" (who dies) give the contrast plainly, as the English "immortal" and "mortal" do.

source.text: Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς, οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore handed over them the God in the desires of the hearts of them to impurity of the to be dishonored the bodies of them among them, \v 25 who exchanged the truth of the God in the lie, and worshiped and served the creation beyond the [one] having created, who is blessed into the ages; amen.

en.L: Therefore God handed them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies were dishonored among them, \v 25 [they] who exchanged the truth of God for the lie and worshiped and served the creation rather than the one who created [it], who is blessed forever. Amen.
en.B: So God handed them over, in the cravings of their hearts, to impurity, and they dishonored their bodies with one another. \v 25 They traded the truth about God for the lie. They bowed down to the creation and served it, instead of the one who created it, who is blessed forever. Amen.
en.R: So God handed them over to the impure things their hearts wanted, and they dishonored their bodies with one another. \v 25 They traded the truth about God for a lie. They worshiped and served the things God made, instead of God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, who made them. Praise belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever! Amen.

es.L: Por lo cual Dios los entregó en los deseos de sus corazones a [la] impureza, de modo que sus cuerpos fueran deshonrados entre ellos, \v 25 [ellos] que trocaron la verdad de Dios por la mentira, y adoraron y sirvieron a la creación antes que a aquel que [la] creó, el cual es bendito para siempre. Amén.
es.B: Por eso Dios los entregó, en los fuertes deseos de sus corazones, a la impureza, y deshonraron sus cuerpos unos con otros. \v 25 Trocaron la verdad acerca de Dios por la mentira. Se postraron ante la creación y le sirvieron, en lugar de servir a aquel que la creó, que es bendito para siempre. Amén.
es.R: Por eso Dios los entregó a las cosas impuras que deseaban sus corazones, y deshonraron sus cuerpos unos con otros. \v 25 Cambiaron la verdad acerca de Dios por una mentira. Adoraron y sirvieron a las cosas que Dios hizo, en lugar de adorar a Dios mismo, que las hizo. ¡A {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le corresponde la alabanza para siempre! Amén.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi Dieu les a livrés, dans les désirs de leurs cœurs, à l’impureté, de sorte que leurs corps ont été déshonorés entre eux, \v 25 [eux] qui ont échangé la vérité de Dieu contre le mensonge et ont adoré et servi la création plutôt que celui qui [l’]a créée, qui est béni pour les siècles. Amen.
fr.B: Dieu les a donc livrés, dans les convoitises de leur cœur, à l’impureté, et ils ont déshonoré leur corps les uns avec les autres. \v 25 Ils ont troqué la vérité sur Dieu contre le mensonge. Ils se sont prosternés devant la création et l’ont servie, au lieu de celui qui l’a créée, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui est béni pour toujours. Amen.
fr.R: Alors Dieu les a livrés aux choses impures que désirait leur cœur, et ils ont déshonoré leur corps les uns avec les autres. \v 25 Ils ont échangé la vérité sur Dieu contre un mensonge. Ils ont adoré et servi ce que Dieu a fait, au lieu de Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, qui l’a fait. Louange à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour toujours ! Amen.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo Mungu aliwakabidhi katika tamaa za mioyo yao kwa uchafu, ili miili yao ivunjiwe heshima miongoni mwao, \v 25 [wao] waliobadilisha kweli ya Mungu kwa ule uongo, wakaviabudu na kuvitumikia viumbe kuliko yule aliyeviumba, ambaye ni mbarikiwa milele. Amina.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Mungu aliwakabidhi kwa uchafu, katika tamaa kali za mioyo yao, nao wakaivunjia heshima miili yao wao kwa wao. \v 25 Walibadilisha kweli kuhusu Mungu kwa ule uongo. Waliinamia viumbe na kuvitumikia badala ya yule aliyeviumba. Yeye ndiye wa kuhimidiwa milele. Amina.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Mungu aliwakabidhi kwa mambo machafu ambayo mioyo yao ilitamani, nao wakaivunjia heshima miili yao wao kwa wao. \v 25 Walibadilisha kweli kuhusu Mungu kwa uongo. Waliabudu na kutumikia vitu ambavyo Mungu aliviumba, badala ya kumwabudu Mungu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliyeviumba. Sifa ni {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} milele! Amina.
